feature: Perspective pill and a shadow that grows with depth
summary: In 3D a pill beside the mode chip shows the camera's perspective. Drag it sideways (or Option-drag an edge pill) to change it for every 3D layer, with dashed lines to the vanishing point, or click it for None, Subtle, Normal, Strong and a slider. A layer pulled forward now casts a larger, softer shadow, and one pushed back a tighter one.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. A picture with a drop shadow (Effects, +, Shadow), picked with the Select tool. The walk is Scripts/playtest/perspective-pill-walk.json.

try.do: Click the cube on the chip by the turn knob to go to 3D, then drag the right edge pill to tip the card. A pill reading 45° sits beside the chip.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Drag the 45° pill sideways. Watch the card and the dashed lines from its corners to its vanishing point.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Hold Option and drag an edge pill sideways: the perspective changes instead of the tip. Press Command Z once.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click the pill: pick Strong, then drag the slider. Press Escape to close it.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press F8 (or the Info button at the end of the tool bar): the same presets and slider sit under Perspective, All 3D layers.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Drag the grip below the card up to pull it forward, then down past where it started to push it back. Compare the shadow.

evaluate: Does a sideways drag on the pill feel like the right speed (a degree for every two points), and Option on an edge pill (a degree for every three)?
Do the dashed lines to the vanishing point help you see what the perspective is doing, or are they noise?
Is the forward shadow growth strong enough to read as depth (it doubles every 200 points forward), or should it grow faster?
Should a 3D layer with no shadow of its own gain one when pulled forward? Today only a shadow it already has grows.
Is the Perspective section in the Info popover in the right place, below Reset, given it changes the camera and not the picked layer?
rough: The mock's popover is a dark plate; this one wears the tool bar's glass so it matches the Info popover beside it, following your call on 2026-10-12 that the Info popover wear the tool bar's own material (that call was about the Info popover; say if this one should be dark).

The mock's popover line 'The camera's, so it changes every 3D layer. Drag the pill sideways to scrub.' is over the chrome budget; its meaning is in the header's 'All 3D layers' and the pill's hover tag 'Perspective · all 3D layers' (UX-PATTERNS §4).

The app goes further than the mock on the vanishing point: the prototype draws its lines to a made-up spot above the card, and these go to where the card's receding edges really meet, which also comes nearer as the perspective strengthens.

The app goes further than the mock on the shadow: the prototype's cards keep one fixed shadow at every depth. Measured with a 4 point blur, 8 point drop shadow on a 100 by 60 card: it reaches 6 rows below the card pushed back 200, 14 flat and 26 pulled forward 200 (before this change, 14 at every depth).

The walk does not press the preset buttons or the sliders in either popover: a walk's press on a SwiftUI button over the canvas does nothing today, a real posted click included (the open task a-walk-s-press-on-a-picture-tile-swatch-or-colou, which now lists this walk). The pill, its scrub, Option on an edge pill, the click that opens the popover and both popovers' values are walked by pointer.
At strong perspective a card near the camera runs well past the canvas and its outline crosses the tool bar; that is the camera doing what it is told, and not changed here.
All pictures except the shadow pair were taken with the window behind another app; the shadow pair is the walk's own render of the canvas, cropped at the card's lower right corner.
